objectified_fact_types.description: The relationship between a Reviewer and a Paper is objectified as Review. A Review represents the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper. This objectification is appropriate because the review is explicitly treated as a business entity with its own identifier (review_id) and attributes (review_score), separate from just recording which reviewer reviewed which paper.

ambiguities.description: Relationship between Reviewer and Paper through Review: The transcript describes reviewers reviewing papers with the constraint that 'a given reviewer reviews a given paper at most once.' This is modeled as an external uniqueness constraint across 'Reviewer conducts Review' and 'Paper is reviewed in Review'. However, it is unclear whether a direct binary fact type 'Reviewer reviews Paper' should also exist in the model, or whether all reviewer-paper interactions should flow exclusively through the Review entity. The current model only expresses the constraint through the objectified Review, which is semantically correct but may not capture the full business intent if direct reviewer-paper tracking is also needed.

ambiguities.description: Temporal state of reviews: The transcript mentions 'completed review' on line 7, which may imply that a review has a lifecycle (e.g., draft, in-progress, completed). It is unclear whether the Review entity tracks only completed reviews or whether incomplete reviews are also modeled. If review state is important, additional attributes or subtypes may be needed.
